newsitem.title: INDIA: Pardoned British model contemplates social work.
newsitem.headline: Pardoned British model contemplates social work.

text.p: British model Samantha Slater, released after two years in jail on a drugs charge in India's southern state of Kerala, said she planned to quit modelling and concentrate instead on social work.

"I may or may not return to modelling. I might do other things like social work," the 25-year-old brunette from Birmingham in central England told reporters late on Saturday night soon after her release from prison.
Slater was released on Thursday, following a mercy petition and signature campaign by her mother in Britain. An Indian bishop also intereceded with authorities on her behalf.
Police arrested Slater, 25, in January 1994 for carrying two ounces of cannbis resin hidden in her brassiere while on a motorbike tour of Kerala with a companion, Andrew Kershaw.
Slater pleaded not guilty to the charges, but was sentenced to 10 years' imprisonment under India's Narcotics Control Act. Kershaw was sentenced to three.
Wearing an embroidered Indian tunic and traditional tight trousers, Slater threw up her arms when she arrived at Madras airport, on her way to the British high commission.
"I am free and glad to be in Madras," she exclaimed. "I thank God and the Kerala governor for setting me free."

Two years in a small town jail in India was a great learning experience, Slater said. She had undergone a cultural transformation while sharing a cell with Indian prisoners, she said, which strengthened her religious feeling.
"I was impressed with the works of Sai Baba (an Indian religious teacher) and read the Bible twice over. I do not regret making the trip to India."
Slater was accompanied by Claire Lewis, a British high commission official, after her release from a jail in Thrissur in Kerala.
The steady prison diet of banana curry and rice got on her nerves, Slater said.
"I did get a lot of concessions though I performed the prison chores like others," she said.
Slater's appeals to the Kerala high court and India's supreme court were turned down.
But the mercy petition to the Kerala governor coupled with the intervention of a local bishop, Joseph Mar Koorilos, aided her release.

Earlier, British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind and other diplomats had pressed for her release because the sentence was considered severe in relation to the small amount of the drug found in her possession.
Karshaw continues to serve his term in a jail in the Kerala state capital, Thiruvananthapuram.
